description: A placeholder such as `T` in `List<T>` that the caller fills with a real type, checked at compile time and kept at run time without type erasure.
A `where` clause such as `where T : class, IEntity` that limits the allowed type arguments and lets the generic code use their members.
A type-safe reference to a method that can be stored, passed and invoked like a value.
The built-in generic delegates: `Func<..., TResult>` returns its last type argument, and `Action<...>` returns nothing.
Inline function syntax such as `p => p.Price > 10` that converts to a delegate or to an expression tree.
A lambda that captures an outer variable itself, not a snapshot, so it sees later changes and keeps the variable alive as long as the delegate lives.
An `Expression<Func<...>>` that represents a lambda as data, which query providers such as EF Core translate into SQL.
A delegate member that outside code can only subscribe to with `+=` and unsubscribe from with `-=`, raised synchronously by its declaring class.
